review_notes: I read the whole file (lines 1–107). Its proofs are short and each does different work. initialForwardChart_continuousAt is a case split plus a differentiability argument. mappedFutureRaw_continuousAt is a composition of continuous maps. mappedFutureRaw_tendsto proves that scaling by a positive constant preserves 𝓝[>] 0. mappedFutureArc_upper is an ite rewrite plus a membership lemma. The only overlap is that mappedFutureRaw_continuousAt and mappedFutureArc_upper both call slitFuturePoint_mem_domain together with future_scaled_offset. That is a two-lemma combination, not substantial repeated reasoning, and future_scaled_offset already factors out the arithmetic. The nhdsWithin scaling step in mappedFutureRaw_tendsto looks like a standard pattern. A grep of the SLE directory found similar tendsto_nhdsWithin_iff uses elsewhere, but I did not confirm any identical nontrivial repeated block, and a shared lemma would be a thin wrapper over existing API. I found no justified finding under this rubric. The one uncertainty is that I did not inspect other files for exact duplicates of the scaling-tendsto proof.
